what: Validation discipline for closed-source npm publishes: always run end-to-end scenarios against an install-from-tarball (NOT against source dir + dev node_modules). This session caught TWO critical bugs that static code review alone missed: (1) missing MCP server bundle (`dist/memory/cli.js`) — would have shipped a "working" tarball where `aide-memory init` succeeds but the MCP server fails silently on first use, (2) dev-monorepo package.json leak in CLI bundle — visible only after extracting a real tarball and grepping the minified output. Workflow that works: `cp package.json /tmp/dev.json && cp package.aide-memory.json package.json && npm pack && mv /tmp/dev.json package.json`, then `npm install ./aide-memory-*.tgz` into a fresh scratch project, then exercise CLI + MCP + hooks. Running CLI/tests from the dev worktree with full dev node_modules hides these classes of bugs because the full tsc output + all dev deps are present. Time cost: ~10 min for a full install-and-scenario pass. Value: catches packaging bugs before they hit users.
why: Both bugs caught this session were invisible in dev-mode testing. Install-from-tarball is the only way to test what users actually get. Future releases should adopt this as a required step (already added to docs/RELEASING.md Step 4 smoke-test section).
